title: EXP01 — Direct prediction of episode onset
objective: Compare direct episode-onset probability with monthly-excess probability under a matched false-onset-alert budget.
hypothesis: Direct onset prediction detects more evaluable onsets than monthly-excess prediction at the same false-alert budget.

execution.authorization: Separate protocol-, commit- and data-bound approval by Mauricio and an independent reviewer is required. Synthetic runs never authorize real fits.

architecture.decision: Add one modular EXP01 experiment pipeline because paired excess and onset objectives change the training graph semantics. Reuse the existing Stage 3 feature derivation, Stage 4 family adapters and Stage 5 sigmoid adapter. Keep label/cohort/metric functions pure. Do not duplicate data ingestion, preparation, training or evaluation pipelines.
architecture.real_pipeline_status: not executable in this delivery; implement and review only after separate human authorization
architecture.profile_decision: A profile on the existing single-target training pipeline cannot express and pair the two target definitions safely.

labels.excess: General dengue count strictly above same-calendar-month prior-five-year type-7 P75; all epidemic years retained.
labels.eligibility: Both horizons require observed Y(T)=0 and predictors available by close of T. Unknown Y(T) is operationally ineligible.
labels.t2: Y(T+1)=0 and Y(T+2)=1; only Y(T)=0 determines operational eligibility.
labels.t1_onset_in_t2: Keep origins with Y(T)=0,Y(T+1)=1 as negatives for exact T+2 onset, including continued episodes. Never retrospectively remove them from the operational cohort.
labels.missing_months: Exact calendar keys only. Missing predecessor, outcome or required historical month yields unavailable label; no interpolation or bridging.
labels.evaluation_evaluability: Post-outcome evaluability is separate from operational eligibility. Both arms use identical evaluable intersections; report excluded/unknown support without treating unknown as zero.

temporal.consumed_2025: Excluded from all input, fitting, calibration, search, thresholds, selection and EXP01 evaluation. Any later separate reference must be named consumed retrospective benchmark.
temporal.stress_2024: Retrospective stress only, known epidemic year; never model/configuration selection or blind confirmation.
temporal.prospective: A truly unobserved later period must be separately reserved and authorized.
temporal.channel: Recompute five prior-year same-month percentiles for each origin/target; reference observations must be <= origin. No supplied precomputed labels/channel are consumed.
temporal.predictor_availability: Every frozen predictor is a T-or-earlier feature (maximum month offset 0). The ordered allowlist and explicit offset are checked before each interface call. Retrospective consolidated inputs cannot establish actual publication latency; operational availability remains a real-run precondition.
temporal.roles: Target-time partitions; calibration/selection/evaluation origins must be >= prior role target-end. Horizon-dependent boundary embargo is reported as coverage, not silently backfilled.
temporal.transformations: Deterministic past-only Stage 3 features; native Stage 4 model adapters fit their existing train-only preparer on training X. Sigmoid fit exclusively on out-of-time calibration. No outer-train refit after calibration.

comparison.historical_EXP00: Not exactly compatible: published 912-row/horizon predictions have consumed 2025 targets; EXP01 uses pre-2025 rolling cohorts and exact-onset risk sets. Do not read/reuse private predictions or claim equivalence.
comparison.excess_comparator: New monthly-excess arm under the same EXP01 rows, ordered predictors, families, fixed parameters, windows, seed and calibration method; not trained in infrastructure delivery.
comparison.paired: One EXP01 parent; arm objective is excess or onset. Paired keys, predictor bytes, missingness and operational cohorts must agree. Probability metrics use each arm's fitted target; onset alert utility uses the common onset label.
comparison.budget: Full development false-onset-alert frontier: all integer budgets 0..number of evaluable negative selection rows. Same cap in both arms, whole score ties, optimize selection onset detections, then fewer false alerts, fewer total alerts, higher threshold. No budget or configuration is chosen from evaluation/stress outcomes.
comparison.realized_burden: Selection caps are equal, realized evaluation false alerts can differ. Report paired realized burden and do not claim equal realized burden merely because development caps match.
comparison.aggregation: Separate horizon, family, window and budget; equal weight development windows only for descriptive summaries. Stress reported separately. No post-hoc best-window/budget/model selection.

design.family_choice: First predeclared configuration of each Stage 4 family, fixed before EXP01, not selected from 2024/2025; no hyperparameter search.
design.calibration: Same sigmoid implementation from Stage 5 per arm/family/horizon/window, fitted on separate out-of-time calibration predictions. Single-class calibration fails; no identity fallback in real execution.
design.fit_count: 3 windows x 3 families x 2 horizons x 2 targets. One fit per arm/window; no search, outer refit or fit per budget.

population.scope_source: Stage 7 demonstrative fixture municipality inventories (public DANE codes, not outcomes).
population.operational: Non-excess at origin in both horizons; all required predictors available by T.
population.availability: Retrospective consolidated data cannot prove historical operational availability; real preflight requires reviewer acknowledgement. No future observation or reporting completeness inferred.

metrics.primary: Paired difference in onset sensitivity across the full matched-development-budget frontier, with realized false-alert burden alongside.
metrics.false_alert_definition: Primary onset false alert means no onset at exact target, including continuing excess. Also report monthly-excess false-alert ratio for the legacy 5pp guardrail.
metrics.episode: One onset is a known 0->1 transition at exact calendar S-1/S; continued months never add episodes. Each horizon reported independently; missing prediction counts as missed onset, not lost denominator.
metrics.probability: Grouped-tie noninterpolated AP (PR-AUC convention), Brier and complementary AUROC per fitted objective. Calibration curves use ten equal-width bins; no model ranking by AUROC.
metrics.uncertainty: Paired municipality cluster x contiguous calendar-year block bootstrap, 1000 replicates, seed 42, percentile 95% intervals; fewer than two municipalities or years explicitly insufficient. Stress-2024 single-year intervals unavailable; no IID row bootstrap.

acceptance.authority: DEC-125, DEC-128 and explicit EXP01 request
acceptance.primary: EXP01's primary comparison is the paired onset-sensitivity difference over the full frozen frontier of equal false-onset-alert caps. DEC-125's 10 pp point criterion is defined against persistence and is not transferred to the direct-onset versus excess head-to-head comparison. No approved numerical superiority threshold exists for this new head-to-head; report the frontier and defer a scientific decision to human review.
acceptance.secondary: DEC-125's five-percentage-point maximum increase in false-alert ratio is a secondary guardrail only against its stated persistence reference, if that exact persistence comparator and denominator are available under an authorized compatible design. It is not an onset-versus-excess allowance and cannot relax the matched-budget primary comparison.
acceptance.uncertainty: Point criteria without dependence-aware support remain insufficient_evidence. All scientific conclusions require human review.

reproducibility.dependencies: Exact pins in pyproject.toml and exported constraints
reproducibility.input_identity: Hash input bytes before and after execution; configuration/protocol/code/runtime hashes in receipt, no raw data in MLflow.
reproducibility.freeze: Canonical sorted compact finite UTF-8 JSON plus newline. Subsequent scientific change requires a new protocol/experiment version or explicit human authorization; never overwrite the expected hash silently.
